incident-bot: ALERT: Inference API (us-west-2) p99 latency spike > SLO threshold for last 6m. Paging oncall @maya. auto-escalate P1 if not ack in 5.

maya (oncall): acked. I'm on it. Paging order? any downstream alerts? :eyes:

lia: seeing p95=320ms (ok) p99=1.9s (breach). error rate for streaming sessions up ~4% last 10m. Query used: promql: rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{handler=~"/v1/generate.*"}[5m]) and histogram_quantile(0.99, ...). attaching graph link: https://grafana.company/r/ABC123

ashok: noticed a flurry of 429s from control-plane config fetch service in the logs. sample:
```
2026-03-14T05:10:12Z GET /config/fetch 429 upstream="config-service" x-rate-limit-remaining=0
```
when config fetch is throttled runtime falls back to live verification path, which adds latency and stalls streaming.

eng-mateo: I see correlated traces: trace id 0a1b2c3d linking generate -> token-auth -> config-fetch -> db-auth. token-auth latencies spiking to 600ms and config-fetch 700-900ms. stack shows retries from client causing queueing in runtime. example span dump: span(token-auth).duration=612ms span(config-fetch).duration=842ms

sre-jen: likely root cause is config-service hitting its per-tenant rate limiter + DB auth contention. Two immediate mitigations:
 1) bump config-service rate limit for internal control-plane calls (emergency override)
 2) enable local cached config fail-open for affected routes
 3) route heavy streaming traffic to fallback model/replica group with lower memory but faster path
I'll run 1 & 2 if ops agree.

maya (oncall): do it. are there customers impacted? severity P1 -> customers may see streaming stalls and higher tail latency.

pm-owen: Customer impact: 3 enterprise tenants on Dedicated in us-west-2 reported slow streaming / stalled sessions. SLA impact: p99 exceeded for last 12m. We should notify CSMs if mitigation >30m.

ashok: applying emergency rate-limit bump to config-service. Kong admin call:
```
curl -s -X PATCH https://kong-admin.internal/services/config-service/ratelimit \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KONG_ADMIN' \
  -d '{"limits":{"per_minute":5000}}'
```
Response: 200 OK. I also set X-Feature-Flag: "config_local_cache_failopen" = true for runtime via ff-service:
```
curl -X POST https://ff.internal/toggles -d '{"flag":"config_local_cache_failopen","state":"on","scope":"us-west-2"}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy rollback to config-service v1.4.2 -> v1.4.1 started by eng-mateo. rollout id: r-20260314-75

eng-mateo: also scaled config-service deployment from 3 -> 8 replicas in cluster us-west-2:
```
kubectl -n controlplane scale deployment/config-service --replicas=8
```
Confirming pods coming up, readiness ok.

lia: after those changes p99 dropped to 480ms within ~3m. error rate normalized to 0.6%. graphs: https://grafana.company/r/ABC123?var-zoom=3m

maya (oncall): great. any other knock-on effects? do we need to evict stuck streaming sessions or restart runtime nodes?

sre-jen: not yet. we should avoid mass restarts. runtime queue drained after rate bump + scale. traces show no more token-auth retries. I want to keep config_local_cache_failopen enabled for 30 minutes then flip to monitored.

eng-mateo: rolled the routing fallback to reduce streaming model weight from 100% -> 60% and route 40% to smaller b-model:
```
PATCH /routing
{"route":"/v1/stream","policy":{"weights":{"main-model":0.6,"b-model-fast":0.4}}}
```
This reduced per-request KV cache pressure.

ashok: verified config-service returned fewer 429s (tail logs):
```
05:22:43 GET /config/fetch 200 upstream="config-service" x-rate-limit-remaining=413
```

pm-owen: I'll draft a short customer note for CSMs: impacted tenants, mitigation actions, ETA for postmortem.

maya (oncall): handing off to @ashok for next shift at 05:30 PST. checklist for handoff:
 - monitor p95/p99 in us-west-2
 - keep config_local_cache_failopen on until further notice
 - rollback routing change if we see correctness issues
 - run smoke tests for streaming for a sample tenant
 - assign postmortem owner

ashok: taking handoff. I'll keep alerts tightened: p99 > 1s -> P1 auto, p99 > 700ms -> high.

sre-jen: add postmortem owner: eng-mateo. please include timeline, root cause (rate limiter + DB auth contention), and long-term fixes: rate-limit backpressure strategies, graceful degrade, and more aggressive local caching.

eng-mateo: assigned. rough RCA note: sudden spike in control-plane config fetch traffic from health-check misconfiguration in a customer integration + DB auth connection pool limit. Suggested fixes: connection pool autosizing, request coalescing for config fetch, per-tenant quotas with early fail-over to cached configs.

lia: leaving final numbers for the incident window (05:07 - 05:27 UTC): total requests affected ~12.3k, error increase from 0.2% -> 4.1%, p99 peak 1.94s, p99 after mitigation 0.48s.

pm-owen: noted. I'll prepare CSM brief and external comms draft.

maya (oncall): thx team. :thumbsup: closing page, handoff complete. I'll file an incident ticket and link this thread.

incident-bot: Incident P1 closed (mitigated). Duration 20m. Postmortem owner: eng-mateo. Link: https://incidents.company/INC-20260314-21

ashok: leaving a reminder: revert emergency ratelimit bump to normal schedule in 45m and toggle off config_local_cache_failopen after validations.

eng-mateo: acked. will include the revert steps in the postmortem.

maya (oncall): follow-up: postmortem due EOD, please attach traces and queries used. handing off monitoring to oncall-next.

deploy-bot: rollback complete for config-service to v1.4.1 -> 100% healthy.

sre-jen: final note: recommend an automated circuit-breaker at runtime to prevent retries piling onto control-plane and to prefer cached configs for short TTLs. Will add to backlog.

maya (oncall): end of thread.
_meta: generated by dataset synthesis: incident thread about latency spike due to control-plane config fetch and auth rate limits, includes mitigation steps, commands, and handoff
